boxer_table_singleton.unresolved_fields: Everything at +0xC and beyond +0x10 that was not directly exercised by the two consumer functions examined in this pass.

traced.proven_behavior: Masks its single argument to 8 bits ($a0 & 0xFF) -- this is a directly proven, concrete fact: the boxer index/ID parameter accepted by this accessor is 8 bits wide. It then calls the singleton accessor and walks a linked list starting from the returned singleton, dereferencing each visited node's +0x10 field up to 'index' times, stopping early if a node is null.
traced.unresolved_question: Whether each node visited by this walk is one boxer record, one loaded-table-instance registration, or some other chained object -- see the RUNTIME_BLOCKED entry in static-resolution-matrix.json.

traced.proven_behavior: Calls the singleton accessor, then passes the result into a second shared generic function (func_001A0D78) not disassembled in this pass.

Calls the singleton accessor, then constructs a separate object (not the singleton itself) that stores a pointer to a fixed data address (D_005817D4) and clears one byte field, then calls another function (func_00186284). Shape is consistent with a cursor/view/query object constructor rather than a direct record reader.

consumers.notes: These 5 functions (plus the loader trampoline itself) are exactly the complete set of direct callers of func_00186408 found by a whole-binary text search across all 24,576 disassembled functions in BOOT.BIN. No other function in BOOT.BIN references the boxer table singleton accessor by name; a caller could in principle still reach the singleton indirectly through one of these 5, or the singleton's raw address (0x80B4) could be hardcoded elsewhere without going through the accessor -- a direct-address search found zero such references, but that does not rule out access via a relocated pointer computed at runtime.

fixed_counts_and_limits.claim: Boxer index/ID parameter to func_00186464 is masked to 8 bits (0-255).
fixed_counts_and_limits.caveat: This proves the accessor's own parameter width, not the database's own record-count field (see xdbboxr-schema.json word0=121, unconfirmed as a record count).

cross_resource_relationships.relationship: preload/tables.viv hairstyle files <-> preload/bootpreloads.viv HK_*.bh preload descriptors
cross_resource_relationships.evidence: 8 of bootpreloads.viv's members (HK_ali.bh, HK_hatto.bh, HK_lazca.bh, HK_leona.bh, HK_moral.bh, HK_pacqu.bh, HK_punch.bh, HK_robin.bh) share name stems with 8 of tables.viv's boxer-surname .txt files (ali.txt, hatton.txt, lazcano.txt, leonard.txt, morales.txt, pacquiao.txt, punchout.txt, robinson.txt). All 7 real-boxer-named pairs correspond to widely-known historical/legend boxers (Ali, Hatton, Lazcano, Leonard, Morales, Pacquiao, Robinson); 'HK_punch'/'punchout.txt' does not match a real boxer name and is plausibly a placeholder/test entry rather than a licensed legend.
cross_resource_relationships.why_not_stronger: No executable code path connecting these two archives was traced in this pass; the relationship rests on name-stem matching alone, which the evidence standard explicitly treats as insufficient for anything above CANDIDATE.

cross_resource_relationships.evidence: Both archives contain the identical 167 member names in the identical order with identical per-member sizes. scripts.viv's members are RefPack-compressed; scrptpal.viv's are not. For the sampled member 'addanims.bin', decompress_refpack(scripts.viv member) and the raw scrptpal.viv member are the same length (248 bytes) and share the same 4-byte magic ('stp\x01') plus most byte positions, but differ at specific integer fields (e.g. a length-like field is 0x4E3 in scripts.viv's decoded copy versus 0x413 in scrptpal.viv's raw copy). This proves the two archives hold two distinct, same-shaped parameter sets for the same named script entries -- not that one is a decompressed duplicate of the other.
cross_resource_relationships.open_question: Why two parameter sets exist (difficulty variant, palette/style variant, or a before/after tuning pass) is not decidable from static evidence alone -- see static-resolution-matrix.json.

cross_resource_relationships.evidence: boxerpre.viv's 8 mor_base_head_dam*.o members (cheek/eye/mouth/nose, left/right) are named for facial damage regions, structurally consistent with the cut/swelling visualization the Medical subsystem's stoppage/damage path would need. No executable code path was traced connecting this archive to any Medical-owning function in this pass.
